description: Cross-binding conformance for an out-of-range const-array gather (esm-spec §4.3.3, CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.5.5 and §5.40). The `index` base is a const array when it is a `const` literal written inline OR an observed defined by one; neither declares a boundary policy, so an index outside 1..N on ANY axis must fail the run with `E_TREEWALK_CONSTARRAY_OOB`. Each case is one document with one assertion, because the fault aborts the whole build or solve. Error cases carry an assertion `expected` of -1, a value no conforming or non-conforming read produces, so a binding that silently returns a number cannot pass by accident. The divergences this closes: Rust decided const-ness by the operand's NAME, so an inline literal took the state gather's zero ghost; Python had no const-array rule in its simulation gather, so index 0 wrapped to the last element and a past-the-end index surfaced as a bare NumPy IndexError; and Julia's run-time const gather checked only the flattened offset, so an overflow on a non-final axis read a neighbouring element. The 2-D cases overflow ONE axis each, on the first axis (whose column-major offset stays in range) and on the second (whose row-major offset stays in range), so a flat-offset-only check fails at least one of them in either memory layout.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; `index` has no scalar evaluator and there is no inline-test runner
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; `index` has no scalar evaluator and there is no inline-test runner

fixtures.note: Control: an observed `tbl` defined by a `const` array, read in range at 4 of 5.
an observed `tbl` defined by a `const` array, read at index 0. A binding that lets a 0-based container wrap it reads the last element (50).
an observed `tbl` defined by a `const` array, read one past the end. A binding that applies the state gather's zero ghost reads 0.
Control: an observed `tbl` defined by a `const` array, 3 rows x 2 columns, read at (3, 2). `value[i][j]` is element (i, j).

an observed `tbl` defined by a `const` array, read at (4, 1): past the end of the FIRST axis only. Its column-major flat offset (4) lies inside the 6 elements, so a check on that offset alone reads another element.

an observed `tbl` defined by a `const` array, read at (1, 3): past the end of the SECOND axis only. Its row-major flat offset (3) lies inside the 6 elements, so a check on that offset alone reads another element.
